84:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Inshiqaq Malik narrated from Abdullah ibn Yazid from Abu Salamah that Abu Hurayrah recited to them When the sky is split and prostrated during it. When he finished, he told them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prostrated during it. Muslim and al-Nasa’i narrated it from Malik through his chain of transmission. Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Nu’man narrated to us, Mu’tamir narrated to us from his father, from Bakr, from Abu Rafi’, who said: I prayed the Isha prayer with Abu Hurayrah and he recited When the sky is split and prostrated. I said to him. He said: I prostrated behind Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I will continue to prostrate during it until I meet him. This was also narrated from Musaddad from Mu’tamir through his chain of transmission. Then he narrated it from Musaddad from Yazid ibn Zari’ from al-Taymi from Bakr from Abu Rafi’ and mentioned it. It was narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi. Muslim and the Sunan scholars narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah. Al-Nasa’i and Sufyan al-Thawri both added, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Musa, on the authority of ‘Ata’ ibn Mina’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: We prostrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during When the heaven is split and Read in the name of your Lord who created. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God Almighty says: When the heaven is split open and that is on the Day of Resurrection and gives ear to its Lord meaning: it listens to its Lord and obeys His command regarding what He commanded it to do regarding the splitting open, and that is on the Day of Resurrection and it is right meaning it is right for it to obey His command because He is the Great Who cannot be resisted or overcome, rather He has subdued everything and everything is humbled before Him. Then He says: And when the earth is spread out meaning: it is spread out, spread out and expanded. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will spread out the earth like a leather cover until there will be no space left for a human being except for his feet. I will be the first to be called, and Gabriel will be at the right of the Most Merciful. By God, he had never seen him before. I will say, 'O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me.' God Almighty will say, 'He has spoken the truth.' Then I will intercede, and I will say, 'O Lord, Your servants worshipped You at the ends of the earth.' He said, 'And it cast out what was within it and was freed from them.'" That is, it cast out what was in its belly of the dead and was freed from them. This was said by Mujahid, Sa'id, and Qatadah. And it obeyed its Lord and was right, as mentioned above. God's statement: O mankind, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion means that you are striving toward your Lord and doing deeds then you will meet Him then you will meet what you have done of good or evil. Evidence for this is what Abu Dawud at-Tayalisi narrated on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja'far on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "Gabriel said, O Muhammad, live as long as you wish, for you will die. Love whatever you wish, for you will be separated from it. Do whatever you wish, for you will meet it." Some people repeat the pronoun in His statement your Lord meaning then you will meet your Lord, meaning that He will reward you for your deeds and recompense you for your striving. Based on this, both statements are interconnected. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: O mankind, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion means: You do a deed with which you will meet God, whether it be good or evil. Qatada said: O man, indeed you are striving toward your Lord with exertion. Indeed, your striving, O son of Adam, is weak, so whoever is able to make his striving in obedience to God, let him do so, and there is no power except with God. Then God the Almighty said: But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, * He will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. That is, easy, without making it difficult, meaning that not all the details of his deeds will be verified, for whoever is brought to account in this way will inevitably perish. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever is called to account will be punished. She said: I said: Did not God the Almighty say: Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. He said: “That is not the reckoning, but that is the presentation. Whoever is called to account on the Day of Resurrection will be punished.” And this is how Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ayoub Al-Sakhtiyani. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, Rawh ibn Ubadah narrated to us, Abu Amir Al-Khazzaz narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: No one will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection except that he will be punished. I said: Doesn’t God say, Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. He said: “That is the presentation. Whoever is questioned about the account will be punished.” And he put his hand on his finger as if to poke fun at it. It was also narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abi Uday, on the authority of Abu Yunus Al-Qushayri, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, and he mentioned the hadith. Both of them narrated it on the authority of Abu Yunus Al-Qushayri, whose name was Hatim ibn Abi Saghira, on his authority. Ibn Jarir said: Nasr ibn Ali Al-Jahdhami narrated to us, Muslim narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn Al-Kharit, the brother of Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Whoever is questioned about the account - or who is brought to account - will be punished. Then she said: The easy reckoning is presented to God, the Most High, and He sees them. Whoever is called to account on that day, O Aisha, will be doomed.’” Sahih according to the criteria of Muslim. And the Almighty’s saying: And he will return to his family, rejoicing, meaning he will return to his family in Paradise. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: Rejoicing, meaning happy and delighted with what God Almighty has given him. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that he said: You are doing deeds that you do not know, and the absent one will soon return to his family, either happy or grieved. God the Almighty said: But he who is given his record behind his back, meaning in his left hand behind his back, his hand is folded behind him and he is given his record with it likewise. He will call for destruction, meaning loss and destruction. “And he will burn in a Blaze. Indeed, he was among his family, rejoicing.” That is, joyful, not thinking about the consequences and not fearing what lay ahead. This brief joy was followed by prolonged sadness. For he thought that he would never return, meaning he believed that he would not return to God and that He would not bring him back after his death. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others. Return means returning. God said: Yes, indeed his Lord is ever Seeing of him, meaning yes, God will bring him back as He began him and will reward him for his deeds, good and bad, for He is All-Seeing of him, meaning All-Knowing, All-Aware.

84:16: It was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Abu Hurayrah, Shaddad ibn Aws, Ibn Umar, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, Makhul, Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, Bakir ibn al-Ashja, Malik, Ibn Abi Dhi’b, and Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majshun that they said: Al-Shafaq is the redness. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Ibn Labiba, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Al-Shafaq is the whiteness. Al-Shafaq is the redness of the horizon, either before sunrise, as Mujahid said, or after sunset, as is well-known among linguists. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: Al-Shafaq is the redness from sunset until the time of the last evening prayer. When it has passed, it is said that the twilight has disappeared. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Shafaq is the remaining light of the sun and its redness at the beginning of the night until close to darkness. Ikrimah said the same, and it is the twilight that occurs between sunset and evening prayer. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The time for sunset is as long as the twilight has not disappeared. All of this is evidence that the twilight is as al-Jawhari and al-Khalil said. However, it is authentically reported on the authority of Mujahid that he said regarding this verse: So I swear by the twilight meaning the entire day. In another narration on his authority, he said the twilight is the sun. Both were narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. What led him to say this was his connection with the verse of God, the Most High: And the night and what it covers, meaning it gathers, as if he swore by light and darkness. Ibn Jarir said: God swore by the day departing and the night advancing. Ibn Jarir said: Others said: The twilight is a name for redness and whiteness, and they said it is one of the opposites. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: And what it covers means what it gathers. Qatadah said: What it gathers of stars and beasts. Ibn Abbas cited as evidence the words of the poet: *Shops, if only they could find a driver* Ikrimah said: And the night and what it covers meaning what it drives of darkness when it is night, everything goes to its place. And the statement of God, And the moon when it is full Ibn Abbas said: When it gathers and is straight. This is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Masruq, Abu Salih, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said. And the moon when it is full when it is straight. Al-Hasan said: When it gathers means when it is full. Qatadah said: When it is round. The meaning of their statement is that when its light is complete and full, he made it opposite to the night and what it covers. And the statement of God, You will surely ascend from one level to another Al-Bukhari said: Sa’id ibn An-Nadr informed us, Hisham informed us, Abu Bishr informed us, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: You will surely ascend from one level to another state after state. He said: This is your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it with this wording. It is possible that Ibn Abbas attributed this interpretation to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if he said: I heard this from your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Thus, his saying your Prophet is in the nominative case as an agent from said, and this is more apparent, and God knows best, as Anas said: “No year will come except that the one after it is worse than it. I heard it from your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Mujahid, that Ibn Abbas used to say: You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: “Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, says one state after another.” This is the wording. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: One level after another is one state after another. This is what Ikrimah, Murrah al-Tayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Masruq, and Abu Salih said. It is possible that what is meant by You will surely ascend from one level to another is one state after another. He said: “This means that what is meant by this is your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace,” so it is in the nominative case, on the basis that this and your Prophet are subject and predicate, and God knows best. Perhaps this is what comes to mind for many of the narrators, as Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Ghandar said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: You will surely ascend from one level to another. He said: “Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” This meaning is supported by the reading of Umar, Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, and most of the people of Mecca and Kufa: You will surely ascend from one level to another with the opening of the ta’ and the ba’. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Shaabi, You will surely ascend from level to level, he said: You will surely ascend, O Muhammad, from heaven to heaven. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, Masruq, and Abu Al-Aaliyah, Level to level, from heaven to heaven. I say: They mean the Night of the Isra’. Abu Ishaq and Al-Suddi said on the authority of a man on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Level to level, from one house to another. And Al-Awfi narrated it similarly on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he added: It is said: One matter after another and One state after another. Al-Suddi himself said: You will surely ascend from level to level, the deeds of those before you, one house after another. I say: It is as if he intended the meaning of the authentic hadith: You will certainly ascend the ways of those who came before you, step by step, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it too. They said: O Messenger of God, do you mean the Jews and the Christians? He said: Then who else? This is possible. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Sadaqah told us, Ibn Jabir told us that he heard Makhul say about the statement of God, You will surely ascend from one level to another, that is, every twenty years you will experience something that you were not experiencing before. Al-A’mash said, Ibrahim told us, Abdullah said, You will surely ascend from one level to another, that is, the sky will crack, then turn red, then change color after color. Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Qays bin Wahb, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud: You will surely ascend from one level to another, that is, the sky will sometimes be like paint and sometimes it will split. Al-Bazzar narrated, on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud: You will surely ascend from one level to another, O Muhammad, meaning one state after another. Then he said: Jabir narrated it on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Sa’id bin Jubayr said, You will surely ascend from one level to another, that is, some people were of lowly status in this world, but they were elevated in the Hereafter. Others were noble in this world, but they were humbled in the Hereafter. Akrima said, Layer after layer means one state after another, a weaned person after being a suckling, and an old man after being a young man. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, Layer after layer means one state after another, prosperity after hardship, and hardship after prosperity, wealth after poverty, and poverty after wealth, health after sickness, and sickness after health. Ibn Abi Hatim said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Zahir, who narrated to me from my father from Amr bin Shammar from Jabir, who is Al-Ja’fi, from Muhammad bin Ali, from Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The son of Adam is in heedlessness of what he was created for. When God, the Most High, wants to create him, He says to the angel, ‘Write his provision, write his lifespan, write his effect. Write whether he is miserable or happy.’ Then that angel is taken away and God sends to him another angel to guard him until he reaches maturity. Then that angel is taken away and God assigns to him two angels to write down his good deeds and his bad deeds. When death comes to him, those two angels are taken away and the Angel of Death comes to him and takes his soul. When he enters his grave, he returns the soul to his body, then the Angel of Death is taken away and the two angels of the grave come and test him. Then they are taken away. When the Hour comes, the Angel of Good Deeds and the Angel of Bad Deeds descend upon him and they pull out a book tied around his neck. Then they come with him, one as a driver and the other as a witness. Then God, the Most High, says, ‘You were in heedlessness of this.’” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, You will surely ride from one level to another. He said, A state after Condition. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is a great matter ahead of you that you cannot comprehend, so seek help from God, the Almighty. This is a rejected hadith and its chain of transmission contains weak people, but its meaning is correct, and God Almighty knows best. Then Ibn Jarir said, after narrating the opinions of the people regarding this verse from the reciters and commentators: The correct interpretation is the opinion of those who said: You, O Muhammad, will surely go through one state after another and one situation after another of hardships.
